links.comparator_used: Other content moderation guardrails (OpenAI Omni Moderation Latest and NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails), not an unfiltered conversational LLM
links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity for detecting mental health crises in text messages, against clinician labels on two datasets
links.effect: VBHSF sensitivity 0.990 and specificity 0.992 on the Verily dataset (1,800 messages). On the Aegis subset (794 messages), sensitivity was 0.982, accuracy 0.921 and specificity 0.859. Sensitivity was significantly higher than both comparators (all p < 0.001). Specificity was higher than NeMo (p < 0.001) but not different from OpenAI Omni Moderation (p = 0.094). The comparators' sensitivity fell below 0.10 for some crisis categories.
links.tradeoff: Specificity fell to 0.859 on the NVIDIA Aegis dataset, compared with 0.992 on the Verily dataset.
links.quote: When compared with the NVIDIA NeMo and OpenAI Omni Moderation Latest guardrails, the VBHSF demonstrated superior performance metrics across both datasets, achieving significantly higher sensitivity in all cases (all p < 0.001) and higher specificity relative to NVIDIA NeMo (p < 0.001), but not to OpenAI Omni Moderation Latest (p = 0.094).

design_hint: crisis-detection safety filter for LLM conversations
